player.speaker: Revolutionary Delegate
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Anna Keller
line.reaction-briliant.text: News of your coastal columns arrived before your train. The stationmaster has already pushed two government troop trains onto sidings; Frankfurt's garrison has spent two days deciding whether it still takes orders.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Anna Keller
line.reaction-tactical.text: The casualty lists reached Frankfurt before you did. The officials have pinned them beside the government's proclamations as proof that your councils can be resisted—and the police guarding this platform believe them.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Anna Keller
line.reaction-victory.text: The northern councils still hold, and their seals got your train through. But Frankfurt is not a naval town: here the old authorities still have police, officials and a printing press.
line.callback-region-secured.speaker: Anna Keller
line.callback-region-secured.text: Four telegrams, four council seals: Norden, Aurich, Emden, Oldenburg. The railwaymen carry your despatches free of charge now and leave the government's sacks on the platform.
line.callback-region-partial.speaker: Anna Keller
line.callback-region-partial.text: This handbill says your coastal rising has already been stopped. It was printed in one of the towns your columns never reached, and the police are passing copies through the barracks.
line.callback-doctrine-rapid.speaker: Anna Keller
line.callback-doctrine-rapid.text: Your speed opened every signal north of here. It also brought me formations that have not slept under a roof since Kiel. Ask them for another forced march and some will make it; do not pretend all will.
line.callback-doctrine-methodical.text: Your column arrived fed, armed and in step. The police used those same hours to wire the telegraph room and promise hot meals in the barracks. We are about to learn which preparation mattered more.
line.frankfurt-platform.speaker: Anna Keller
line.frankfurt-platform.text: Keep your men off the tracks. The locomotive crews have banked their fires. Soldiers tear the imperial cockades from their caps; the police at the telegraph room pretend not to notice. Everyone is waiting for someone else to move first.
line.keller-opening.speaker: Anna Keller
line.keller-opening.text: The railwaymen will stop troop trains for your column, but they will not hand you Frankfurt. Lose these stations and every council delegate in the city becomes a name on a police list. Hold them, and no loyalist company moves without our permission.
line.weber-question.speaker: Otto Weber
line.weber-question.text: One company has elected delegates; another has locked its armoury. The officers promise hot food to anyone who obeys. Until Frankfurt elects a council, the soldiers will follow your field orders. What do they see first: a public council, or the old command losing its machinery?
line.weber-question.choice.take-infrastr: Occupy the Hauptbahnhof, bridges, post and telegraph. Once communications are ours, the authorities cannot coordinate a suppression force.
Gain a prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo the two additional worker battalions.
line.weber-question.choice.declare-counc: Call a mass assembly and proclaim the council before moving on the barracks. Political legitimacy will bring hesitant soldiers over to us.
Raise two worker battalions and earn their later political support, but pay prestige and forgo core-wide experience.
line.adler-infrastructure.speaker: Dr. Jakob Adler
line.adler-infrastructure.role: Municipal Doctor and Relief Liaison — Fictional Composite
line.adler-infrastructure.text: These keys open the municipal flour stores. I will hand them to an elected council, not to the first armed man at the door. Put one of my clerks beside every guard and I will keep bread carts moving while you take the switchboards.
line.keller-infrastructure-answer.text: Keep the keys, Doctor, and send your clerks. The railwaymen will put elected delegates beside our guards. If we do not say whose orders the telegraph carries, fear will answer for us.
line.keller-assembly.speaker: Anna Keller
line.keller-assembly.text: The unions can fill the square before noon, and soldiers who will not follow a secret committee may follow a council elected in front of them. But while the speeches are being made, trusted crews must close the stations to hostile troop movements.
line.weber-assembly-objection.speaker: Otto Weber
line.weber-assembly-objection.text: A public mandate may bring hesitant companies over. It will not stop the troop train already signalled from the west. Give the speeches their square, but if the railway crews wait for the vote before pulling that signal, legitimacy will arrive under guard.
line.adler-assembly.speaker: Dr. Jakob Adler
line.adler-assembly.role: Municipal Doctor and Relief Liaison — Fictional Composite
line.adler-assembly.text: Then let the square elect its council. I have flour for two days and a clinic already short of bandages. Tell the crowd who brings tomorrow's bread before the old officials tell them your speeches stopped it.
line.loyalist-warning.speaker: Loyalist District Command
line.loyalist-warning.text: All railway, postal and municipal facilities are to remain under lawful authority. Armed councils will be dispersed and military property recovered.
line.weber-final.speaker: Otto Weber
line.weber-final.text: Then every company receives the same offer: elect delegates and keep its weapons under council authority, or be disarmed. Frankfurt must choose before Berlin chooses for it—and the railway must carry that choice east.
